title: The role of AI assisted writing feedback in developing secondary students writing skills
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether AI-assisted writing feedback improves the writing performance of secondary-level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students more than traditional teacher feedback alone. The authors focus on a common instructional problem in EFL writing classrooms: teachers often have limited time to provide detailed, individualized feedback, while students need frequent revision opportunities to improve grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and overall writing quality. The study also examines students’ perceptions of using an AI writing assistant as a feedback tool.

The intervention compared two feedback conditions over an 8-week period. The experimental group used Grammarly to receive immediate AI-generated feedback on drafts, including grammar, spelling, punctuation, word choice, style, sentence clarity, and coherence; after revision, the teacher also provided brief higher-order feedback. The control group followed a traditional process in which the teacher provided delayed written feedback on drafts. Both groups completed pre-test and post-test timed persuasive essays and followed the same writing curriculum with the same instructor. Writing was scored analytically across content, organization, language use, and mechanics by two independent EFL raters, and the experimental group also completed a post-study perception questionnaire.

Participants were 60 Turkish public high school students aged 15–17 enrolled in an EFL program, divided into an experimental group and a control group of 30 each. The study took place in a secondary school setting in Türkiye during regular class time, with use of the school computer lab for the AI tool. Students had little prior experience with AI-based writing tools, and parental consent was obtained because participants were minors.

The main conclusion is that AI-assisted feedback significantly improved students’ writing more than teacher-only feedback. The experimental group showed larger gains in total writing scores, especially in language use and organization, while both groups improved over time. Students also reported positive perceptions of the AI tool, including improved confidence and satisfaction with the feedback. The authors conclude that AI writing tools can effectively supplement secondary EFL writing instruction, particularly when combined with teacher guidance rather than used as a replacement for human feedback.

identified_tools.name: Grammarly
identified_tools.description: An AI-driven automated writing evaluation and writing feedback software that provides feedback on grammar, spelling, punctuation, word choice, style, clarity, and coherence.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the AI writing assistant for secondary Turkish EFL students during an 8-week writing intervention. Students uploaded essay drafts to Grammarly, reviewed its immediate feedback, revised their drafts, and then received brief teacher follow-up on higher-order concerns.

findings.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study, students using Grammarly plus brief teacher follow-up improved more in overall writing performance than students receiving teacher-only feedback. The experimental group (n=30) increased from 25.8 (SD=5.4) to 32.9 (SD=4.8), while the control group (n=30) increased from 25.2 (SD=5.1) to 28.6 (SD=5.3); the Group × Time interaction was significant, F(1, 58)=15.27, p<0.001, partial η2=0.21, and gain scores differed significantly, t(58)=4.12, p<0.001, Cohen’s d≈1.06.
findings.measure: Analytic writing assessment total score out of 40 using an adapted Cambridge English B2 Writing Assessment Scale on pre-test and post-test essays

findings.finding_summary: Grammarly-supported students showed greater improvement in Language Use than the teacher-only group. The paper reports a significant Group × Time interaction for Language Use, F(1, 58)=8.92, p<0.01, with the experimental group showing especially notable gains in language use (+2.5).
findings.measure: Language Use sub-score from the analytic writing rubric

findings.finding_summary: Grammarly-supported students also improved more in Organization than the teacher-only group. The Group × Time interaction for Organization was significant, F(1, 58)=4.35, p<0.05, and the experimental group showed notable gains in organization (+1.8).
findings.measure: Organization sub-score from the analytic writing rubric

findings.finding_summary: Students reported favorable perceptions of Grammarly as a feedback tool after the intervention. In the experimental group (n=30), 90% agreed/strongly agreed that the AI feedback helped improve their writing, 87% reported feeling more confident in their writing, 80% wanted to continue using AI writing feedback, and 90% were overall satisfied with the feedback.
findings.measure: Post-study Likert-scale questionnaire on perceived improvement, clarity, confidence, future use, and satisfaction

quality_tier_rationale: This is a primary quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study with a control group and reported statistical tests/effect sizes, but it is not a full RCT and was conducted in a single school with a relatively small sample.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported impact on overall writing performance is large and clearly positive, with Cohen’s d≈1.06 and partial η2=0.21, indicating substantial improvement for the Grammarly-supported group.
